To create a new branch in Git **using the command line**, you have a few primary options.

**1. Create a branch and switch to it immediately (most common)**

This command creates a new branch based on your current `HEAD` (the commit you are currently on) and checks it out in a single step. **Git +1**

[Git](data:image/png;base64,)

**bash**

`git checkout -b <new-branch-name>`

- **Example:** `git checkout -b feature/login-page`

Alternatively, since Git version 2.23+, the `git switch` command is the preferred alternative for this action: **Stack Overflow +1**

[Stack Overflow](data:image/png;base64,)

**bash**

`git switch -c <new-branch-name>`

**2. Create a new branch without switching to it**

This command creates the new branch, but you remain on your current branch. **Git +1**

[Git](data:image/png;base64,)

**bash**

`git branch <new-branch-name>`

- **Example:** `git branch feature/user-profile`

To switch to the new branch later, you would use:

**bash**

`git checkout <new-branch-name>
# or in Git 2.23+
git switch <new-branch-name>`

**3. Create a branch from a specific commit, tag, or another branch**

You can specify a starting point (like another branch name, a commit hash, or a tag) for your new branch. **Stack Overflow +1**

[Stack Overflow](data:image/png;base64,)

**bash**

`git checkout -b <new-branch-name> <start-point>
# or in Git 2.23+
git switch -c <new-branch-name> <start-point>`

- **Example from a specific commit:** `git checkout -b bugfix/hotfix-issue 9fceb02`
- **Example from an existing branch:** `git checkout -b subfeature/button-color feature/login-page`
    
    **Graphite**
    
    [Graphite](data:image/png;base64,)
    

**4. Push the new branch to a remote repository**

A branch created locally only exists on your machine until you push it to a remote repository (like [**GitHub**](https://github.com/) or GitLab). **GitProtect +1**

[GitProtect](data:image/png;base64,)

**bash**

`git push -u origin <new-branch-name>`

The `-u` flag sets the upstream branch, which makes future `git push` and `git pull` commands simpler for that branch. **Better Stack**

[Better Stack](data:image/png;base64,)

For more information, refer to the [**official Git documentation**](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Branching-Basic-Branching-and-Merging) on branching.
